Here are the answers based on the log evidence:

---

### (1) First real error burst — when and which host

The first real error of the outage burst was:

> **`2026-01-18T03:17:42Z` on `api-07`:** `"db pool exhausted (max=20) waiting=14 path=/v1/orders"`

Within seconds this cascaded across all hosts (api-01 through api-08), producing hundreds of 503 errors over the following minutes. The isolated TLS handshake error at `02:41:07Z` on `api-02` was incidental noise — a single peer reset that did not cascade or affect services afterward.

---

### (2) Root cause

**Database connection pool exhaustion.** Services were trying to acquire DB connections from a pool with `max=20`, but all 20 slots were held with none being released. When the web request timeout was exceeded, subsequent requests started returning `503 upstream=db pool exhausted`.

---

### (3) Responsible batch job / user

**`batch-01` running `reconcile-ledger` under user `svc-batch`**

At **`2026-01-18T03:15:03Z`**, this job started and acquired all 20 DB connections from the primary pool. It acquired them 5 seconds apart (from `03:15:04Z` through `03:16:39Z=`) and **never released any of them**. This left zero connections available for the live service traffic, which is why all API hosts hit pool exhaustion starting 2-3 minutes later as their connection timeouts fired and began propagating errors to each other.

---

### Timeline summary

| Time | Event |
|---|---|
| `03:15:03Z` | `batch-01 (svc-batch / reconcile-ledger)` starts, grabs connections 1–20 over the next 96 seconds, holds them all |
| `03:17:42Z` | First web request fails with pool exhaustion on `api-07` (`/v1/orders`) |
| `03:17:43+Z` | Rapid cascade: all API servers (api-01 through api-08) begin returning 503 |
| `03:17–03:18Z` | ~299 additional db pool exhaustion errors across all hosts (the visible portion of the burst) |
